999 and 112: the UK's national emergency numbers - GOV.UK

notes: 999 and 112 calls are answered by a BT call handler who asks "emergency, which service?" and transfers the call to the local police, ambulance, fire or coastguard control room. Source: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/999-and-112-the-uks-national-emergency-numbers, retrieved 2026-09-26.

Phone providers must let any end-user reach the emergency services on 112 and 999 at no charge (Ofcom General Condition A3). Source: https://www.ofcom.org.uk/phones-and-broadband/phone-numbers/cw_996, retrieved 2026-09-26.

Call 999 if a crime is in progress or someone is in immediate danger; 101 is the police non-emergency number. Calls to 999 and 101 are free. Source: https://www.gov.uk/contact-police, retrieved 2026-09-26.

Silent Solution: if you need police but cannot speak, dial 999, cough or tap if you can, and press 55 when prompted to be put through to police. Source: https://www.policeconduct.gov.uk/our-work/key-areas-of-work/silent-solution (Independent Office for Police Conduct), retrieved 2026-09-26.
